source.title: Deep Neural Networks Learn Meta-Structures from Noisy Labels in Semantic Segmentation
source.authors: Yao-Ru Luo; Guo-Le Liu; Wenjing Li; Yuanhao Guo; Ge Yang

record.tranche_reason: Tests noisy-label learning in semantic segmentation, a new setting for the cited classification findings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports noisy-label segmentation outcomes, including comparisons with random labels and learning curves. It does not report training error for random labels. Results from the proposed iGTT method are not rows because they evaluate that method rather than the claim's behavior.
record.test_reason: The study examines random-label learning dynamics and performance under pixel-label corruption in semantic segmentation, extending the classification setting. It does not establish zero training error on random labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: segmentation networks exploit spatial meta-structures preserved by some noisy labels, and disrupting those structures worsens performance. The authors also interpret random-label learning curves as initial pattern learning followed by memorization. That interpretation should remain attributed to them: convergence to a constant loss does not demonstrate perfect random-label fitting.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the label-noise intervention in semantic segmentation with U-Net and DeepLab variants, binary cross-entropy loss, and SGD; pixel-level noise and segmentation metrics differ from the cited classification studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Label type and perturbation strength affect performance; higher random-label generation probability is associated with faster training-loss convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Segmentation performance remains similar when only a randomly sampled subset of correct pixel labels is retained.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Semantic segmentation can tolerate sparse correct pixel supervision.

fits_no_version.finding: Randomly generated labels yield worse segmentation than flipped labels despite having lower pixelwise label error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spatial label structure predicts segmentation generalization better than pixelwise label correctness alone.

record.problems: The paper does not report random-label training error, so whether fitting reaches zero or near-zero training error cannot be determined. Several binary results are plotted rather than numerically tabulated in the supplied text; Appendix results are referenced but not included here.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant numeric results were available in the supplied text. The proposed iGTT method's performance comparison in Table 3 was omitted because it evaluates the authors' new unsupervised method rather than random-label fitting behavior.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero random-label training error, chance-level test performance, and a controlled demonstration that architecture and hyperparameters remain unchanged.
A small constant-factor increase in time to fit random versus true labels; comparable training-error convergence endpoints. The reported slowdown concerns segmentation-performance convergence.
Perfect training fit throughout corruption, a complete trajectory through fully randomized labels, and a quantified chance endpoint.
All regularization interventions and their effects on random-label fitting and clean-label generalization.
Direct tracking of clean versus noisy training-label fitting and direct verification that the late phase memorizes random labels.

missing.what: Convergence rate generally decreases with increasing label randomization, especially for DeepLabv3+. Extract the flipping conditions separately from sampling and identify that the curves measure test Dice.
The main text reports similar two-stage random-label learning on MITO, but no row records this additional dataset. Exact curves are unavailable in the supplied text.
missing.locator: Learning behavior of DNNs Trained by RL; reference to Appendix C.4D

record.verdict_notes: No V1 verdict is justified by the available loss descriptions. Cityscapes sampling probabilities must not be treated as corruption fractions, and its clean baseline is externally cited. The supplied text contains figure captions and qualitative descriptions but no readable numerical curve coordinates.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label conditions are evaluated, but the paper does not state that training error reaches zero or near zero, or report test error at chance.
The paper does not compare training time for fitting true versus fully random labels or report convergence time as a function of corrupted-label fraction.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs are tested.
The paper does not report whether training sets are fit perfectly at each corruption level.
Weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation are not tested as factors in fitting random labels or generalizing on true labels.
The paper tests random labels in segmentation, but does not compare learning of real and random labels using a direct measure of label fitting.

rows.subject: U-Net

rows.measure: Training loss and test dice during training
rows.value: Training loss converges more quickly under a higher generation probability; test dice drops quickly and converges to a low value.
rows.locator: Learning behavior of DNNs Trained by RL; Figure 5C
rows.note: The paper describes the learning curve but does not report random-label training error or exact curve values.
rows.check: Convergence of training loss to an unspecified constant does not establish zero or near-zero training error. Low test Dice is not a demonstrated chance baseline. Generation probability zero produces constant background labels rather than a nondegenerate random labeling.

rows.subject: U-Net and DeepLabv3+
rows.operation_detail: Trained on binary segmentation with randomly sampled or randomly flipped labels.
rows.measure: Final test dice score relative to clean-label training
rows.value: Maximum gap between final dice scores of CL and RCL is 7%.
rows.locator: Existence of Meta-Structures; Figure 2; Appendix C.3 referenced
rows.note: The paper reports the maximum gap in aggregate across the plotted models and says scores decrease only slightly.
rows.check: The reported slight Dice decrease is a small effect in V4's direction, not absence. Split random flipping from sampling, which removes supervision rather than corrupting labels. The aggregate maximum gap of 7% does not identify a particular model, dataset, or corruption level.

rows.subject: U-Net
rows.operation_detail: Trained on ER binary segmentation with random labels while test dice and training loss were tracked.
rows.value: Dice scores fluctuate substantially and reach several high values, then drop quickly and converge to a low value.
rows.locator: Learning behavior of DNNs Trained by RL; Figure 5C
rows.note: Authors interpret the first stage as continued learning before the network is strongly influenced by RL, followed by memorizing as generalization worsens.
rows.check: The reported early high test Dice followed by collapse supports the temporal pattern indirectly. It does not directly measure acquisition of real patterns or subsequent fitting of random labels; separate the degenerate zero-generation condition.
